sources.title: Subnational population projections: 2022-based
sources.verified_claim: ONS identifies the 2022-based datasets as the latest local-authority population projections and states they are widely used in planning. They indicate potential future population size and are not treated as a parcel-level forecast.

sources.title: Subnational population projections for England: 2022-based
sources.verified_claim: ONS states projections are not forecasts, become increasingly uncertain at smaller geographies, and records a correction to several variant datasets after release. Correction and variant status are retained rather than silently ignored.

sources.title: Methodology used to produce the 2022-based subnational population projections for England
sources.verified_claim: ONS documents cohort-component methods, migration assumptions and the use of recent trends, while stating projections generally do not account for policy or development aims not already reflected in observed trends.

sources.title: Subnational population projections QMI
sources.verified_claim: ONS quality guidance describes consistent methods and input sources for local projections. Consistency supports comparison but does not remove uncertainty or make the figures an exact demand estimate for a candidate parcel.

sources.title: Population projections for local authorities by single year of age and sex, England
sources.verified_claim: ONS publishes 25-year local-authority projection data and explicitly notes statistics may be revised or corrected. Dataset availability is not parcel-specific evidence.

sources.title: Household projections for England: 2022-based
sources.verified_claim: ONS labels this the latest household-projection release and states household projections are not predictions of how many homes should be built. Local economic development and housing policy are not included in the projections.

sources.title: Population projections
sources.verified_claim: GLA Demography produces regularly updated trend and housing-led projections for borough, ward and MSOA geographies and explains the uncertainty inherent in demographic modelling. These are planning inputs rather than parcel demand forecasts.

sources.title: Population and household projections
sources.verified_claim: GLA states 2024-based population projections are planned for release in the week commencing 3 August 2026 and provides interim/draft outputs in the meantime. The future release is not treated as already available on 24 July 2026.
